draft.title: Tax and superannuation
card: Income tax
Income tax is taken out of a person's pay and sent to the government. It is a share of what they earn, so it is found by multiplying pay by a percentage.
Superannuation
Super is money an employer pays into a fund for the worker's retirement. It is also a share of earnings, and it is paid on top of the wages, not taken out of them.
Take-home pay = pay − tax. Super is not part of take-home pay, because it goes straight into the fund.
Example: Sam earns $1000 in a week. Tax is 20%, so tax = 0.2 × 1000 = $200 and take-home pay is $800. Super at 10% of $1000 is $100, paid into Sam's fund.
draft.remember: Tax is taken out of pay. Super is paid in addition by the employer, and both are a share of earnings.

a.q: Lena earns $800 in a week. Her tax is 25% of her pay. What is her take-home pay?
a.why: Tax = 0.25 × 800 = $200, and take-home pay = 800 − 200 = $600. The $200 is the tax taken out, not what Lena keeps.
a.clue: Find the tax first, then take it away from the pay.

b.q: Omar earns $2000 a fortnight. His tax is 15% of his pay. His employer pays super of 10% of his pay into a fund. How much does Omar take home?
b.why: Tax = 0.15 × 2000 = $300, so take-home pay = 2000 − 300 = $1700. Super is paid by the employer on top of wages and is not taken from Omar's pay, so the $200 super is not subtracted.
b.clue: Does the super come out of Omar's pay?

problems.detail: The card says income tax 'is found by multiplying pay by a percentage', which suggests Australian income tax is one flat rate. It is actually progressive, with a tax-free threshold and rising marginal rates. A note that the flat rate is a simplification would stop students learning this as fact.

The example uses super at 10%. The Superannuation Guarantee rate has been above 10% since July 2021 and is 12% from 1 July 2025. Students may take 10% as the real rate, so the example should use the current rate or say the rate is made up.

check.summary: Both questions are correct and well built. The card presents income tax as one flat percentage without saying this is a simplification, and its 10% super example is below the current 12% rate.

proposal.title: Tax and superannuation
card: Income tax

Income tax is taken out of pay and sent to the government. Here it is shown as one percentage of pay, a simplification: in real life income above a tax-free amount is taxed at rates that rise as income rises.
Superannuation
Super is money an employer pays into a fund for the worker's retirement. It is a share of earnings set by law, 12% from 1 July 2025, paid on top of wages, not taken out of them.
Take-home pay = pay − tax. Super goes straight into the fund, so it is not part of take-home pay and is not subtracted from it.
Example: Sam earns $1000 in a week, with a simple tax rate of 20%. Tax = 0.2 × 1000 = $200, so take-home pay is $800. Super = 0.12 × 1000 = $120, paid into Sam's fund.
proposal.remember: Tax is taken out of pay. Super is paid in addition by the employer, and both are a share of earnings.

a.q: Lena earns $800 in a week. Her tax is 25% of her pay. What is her take-home pay?
a.why: Tax = 0.25 × 800 = $200, and take-home pay = 800 − 200 = $600. The $200 is the tax taken out, not what Lena keeps.
a.clue: Find the tax first, then take it away from the pay.

b.q: Omar earns $2000 a fortnight. His tax is 15% of his pay. His employer pays super of 12% of his pay into a fund. How much does Omar take home?
b.why: Tax = 0.15 × 2000 = $300, so take-home pay = 2000 − 300 = $1700. The super of 0.12 × 2000 = $240 is paid by the employer on top of wages, so subtracting it as well to get $1460 is wrong.
b.clue: Does the super come out of Omar's pay?
